Fault library

MCB trips under load

The breaker holds at low demand but trips when kettles, heaters, or multiple appliances run together, suggesting thermal overcurrent stress rather than an instant short.

protection-devicesovercurrentsocket-circuits

RCD trips immediately

The RCD drops out as soon as it is reset or as soon as a circuit is energized, indicating leakage or a neutral-earth fault path.

protection-devicesearth-leakagesafety

RCBO trips on one circuit

A single RCBO repeatedly trips, narrowing the issue to one final circuit and allowing focused diagnosis.

rcbosingle-circuitfault-isolation

Some sockets dead, others live

Part of a socket circuit remains energized while other points are dead, often signaling ring discontinuity or localized disconnection.

socket-circuitsring-finalcontinuity

Whole socket circuit dead

All sockets on one circuit are unavailable, pointing to protective device operation, supply interruption, or a major open-circuit fault.

socket-circuitsoutageprotection-devices

Lights not working on one floor

A section of lighting is lost while other lighting remains, suggesting local feed/switch-line/neutral issues.

lightingswitchingneutral-faults

Lights flicker or dim

Brightness fluctuates, especially when appliances start, which may indicate voltage drop, loose connections, or shared neutral issues.

lightingvoltage-dropconnections

Socket or switch feels hot / shows burn marks

Accessory surface heat, discoloration, or burn marks indicate high-resistance contact or overloading and require immediate stop-use behavior.

overheatingfire-riskaccessories

Appliance causes trip when plugged in

A specific appliance repeatedly causes protective-device operation, indicating likely appliance leakage or internal short.

appliance-faultsearth-leakagercd-rcbo

Two-way switching behaves strangely

Lights only work from one location or switch logic feels inverted, commonly due to incorrect strapper/common terminations.

lightingswitchingwiring-logic

Low insulation resistance suspected

Symptoms suggest insulation breakdown such as damp-related leakage, aged cable deterioration, or damaged accessories.

insulationdeteriorationtesting

Loose connection / overheating suspected

Symptoms suggest a high-resistance joint where current flow causes localized heating, voltage drop, and intermittent operation.

connectionsoverheatingfire-risk

Borrowed neutral suspected

Two circuits appear unintentionally interconnected through shared neutral paths, often causing unexplained RCD/RCBO behavior.

neutral-faultslightingcompliance

Broken ring final suspected

Ring continuity loss can leave sockets working but force current down a single leg, creating overload hotspots.

ring-finalcontinuityload-distribution

Damaged cable / exposed cores / unenclosed connection

Visible cable damage or unenclosed joints indicate direct contact and fault-current hazards requiring immediate controls.

cable-damageexposed-live-partsurgent
